titel: Defending the Midterms from Donald Trump

einzeiler: Reporter Barton Gellman on threats to the midterms and pushback from local officials.
kurzfassung: The Trump administration has made numerous attempts to disrupt upcoming elections by demanding voter data and filing lawsuits against state election officials. Despite these unprecedented challenges, federal courts have consistently blocked the administration's efforts, resulting in a string of legal defeats. Meanwhile, local leaders like Utah Lieutenant Governor Deidre Henderson face intense pressure for refusing to comply with federal demands.
stichpunkte: The Justice Department demanded full electronic voter rolls from all 50 states under the guise of cleaning them.
Federal courts have overwhelmingly rejected the administration's lawsuits, leaving the DOJ with an unprecedented 0-27 record in those cases.
Legal experts view the flurry of lawsuits as groundwork for post-election challenges rather than viable attempts to alter current voter rolls.
Utah Lieutenant Governor Deidre Henderson faced severe harassment and threats for refusing to hand over voter data.
Despite intense political pressure, analysts suggest defending state independence may ultimately benefit Henderson politically.
The Justice Department has filed a preemptive lawsuit in Alaska attempting to block election certification if Republican candidates lose.
Tactics like threatening to deploy ICE agents at polling places aim to intimidate voters, particularly in mixed-status Latino families.
Experts remain cautiously optimistic that courts and prepared local officials will successfully counter voter intimidation attempts.

clips.hook: An unprecedented losing streak in federal court
clips.text: The federal government initiated legal action against thirty state election officials, resulting in dozens of consecutive defeats without a single victory.

clips.hook: A complete lack of constitutional authority
clips.text: Judicial opinions have characterized the administration's legal positions as a total disregard for the separation of powers and fabricated authority.
After alleging that tens of thousands of unauthorized individuals were registered to vote, authorities brought charges against a tiny fraction of that number.

clips.hook: Lawsuits designed for a specific outcome
clips.text: The current legal strategy explicitly demands that judges block election results under the single condition that a specific political party loses.
Although historical efforts existed to place law enforcement near polling locations, election administrators today are thoroughly trained to handle interference.

beschreibung:
Amid all the prognostication about which party will emerge triumphant during the midterms, there has also been increasing alarm: Will it be a free and fair election? As soon as Donald Trump returned to office, he began making moves to create disruption—demanding private voter data from states, threatening election officials with jail time, and even seizing ballots from prior elections to investigate alleged fraud. And although, so far, none of the White House’s efforts have threatened to significantly alter the results, the Department of Justice has hinted that there is more to come. The U.S. Attorney General, Todd Blanche, has not ruled out using the force of law to prevent election certifications. Furthermore, a lawsuit from the Trump Administration against the State of Alaska is already under way, before a single vote has even been counted. The reporter Barton Gellman and David Remnick discuss the threats to the midterm elections and Gellman’s new piece, “The State Officials Defending the Midterms from the President.”
Further reading:
“How ICE Is Targeting the 2026 Midterms,” by Jonathan Blitzer
“What the Gerrymandering Wars Mean for the Midterms—and 2028,” by Isaac Chotiner
“The G.O.P.’s Latest Voter-Suppression Plan,” by Sue Halpern
“Donald Trump Already Knows the 2026 Election Is ‘Rigged,’ ” by Susan B. Glasser
